preview.text: Welcome to Mass Adventure! Let’s take a little journey together. At Mass, we gather as God’s family, listen to his Word, and grow closer to Jesus. Take your time. There is so much to discover.

entrance.text: Entrance Procession and Hymn. What is happening? The priest and helpers walk toward the altar. We stand and sing as Mass begins. Why do we do this? We gather as God’s family to worship him. Try it! Stand tall and think of one thing to thank God for.. Big word: Altar. The holy table where the Eucharistic sacrifice is celebrated.

sign.text: Sign of the Cross. What is happening? We make the Sign of the Cross. We begin in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Why do we do this? We remember that we belong to God. Try it! With your right hand, touch your forehead, chest, left shoulder, then right shoulder.

greeting.text: Greeting. What is happening? The priest greets everyone. When he says “The Lord be with you,” we answer “And with your spirit.” Why do we do this? Our words remind us that God is with us. Try it! Ask a grown-up to say “The Lord be with you.” Answer “And with your spirit.”

penitential.text: Penitential Act. What is happening? We remember the times we have done wrong. We ask God for mercy and help to love better. Why do we do this? God invites us to turn back to him. Try it! Quietly tell God you are sorry and ask for help to be kind.

gloria.text: Gloria. What is happening? We sing or say a joyful song of praise. We give glory to God for his goodness. Why do we do this? We praise God because he is wonderful. Try it! Say one short sentence praising God.

collect.text: Opening Prayer (Collect). What is happening? The priest invites us to pray. After a quiet moment, he gathers our prayer into one prayer to God. Why do we do this? We pray together with one heart. Try it! Think of someone to pray for. Then listen and answer “Amen.”. Big word: Collect. The opening prayer that gathers our prayers together.

first.text: First Reading. What is happening? A reader shares words from the Bible, often from the Old Testament. At the end, the reader says “The word of the Lord.” We answer “Thanks be to God.” Why do we do this? God teaches us through Sacred Scripture. Try it! Sit quietly and listen. When the reader says “The word of the Lord,” join in: “Thanks be to God.”

psalm.text: Responsorial Psalm. What is happening? We hear a prayer from the Book of Psalms. We sing or say a response together. Why do we do this? We answer God’s Word with prayer. Try it! Listen for the repeated line and join in.. Big word: Psalm. A prayer or song from the Bible.

second.text: Second Reading. What is happening? On Sundays and special days, we hear another Bible reading, usually from a New Testament letter. At the end, the reader says “The word of the Lord.” We answer “Thanks be to God.” Why do we do this? The apostles help us learn to live with Jesus. Try it! Listen for a way to love God or other people. When the reader says “The word of the Lord,” answer “Thanks be to God.”

alleluia.text: Gospel Acclamation (Alleluia). What is happening? We stand to welcome the Gospel. Usually we sing Alleluia, a word of praise. Why do we do this? We welcome Jesus speaking to us in the Gospel. Try it! Stand and get your listening heart ready.. Big word: Alleluia. A word that means “Praise the Lord!”

gospel.text: Gospel. What is happening? The priest or deacon reads from a Gospel. We hear about Jesus’ words and deeds. Why do we do this? Jesus teaches us how to follow him. Try it! Make a little cross on your forehead, lips, and heart.. Big word: Gospel. The Good News about Jesus.

homily.text: Homily. What is happening? The priest or deacon helps us understand the readings. He shows how they connect to our lives. Why do we do this? God’s Word helps us love in everyday life. Try it! Remember one idea you can try this week.. Big word: Homily. A talk that helps us understand God’s Word.

creed.text: Creed. What is happening? Together, we say what we believe. We speak about the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit, and the Church. Why do we do this? We share the faith of the Church. Try it! Say “I believe” and think of God’s love.. Big word: Creed. A summary of what the Church believes.

faithful.text: Prayer of the Faithful. What is happening? We pray for the Church and the world. We remember people who need God’s help. Why do we do this? God calls us to care for everyone. Try it! Think of someone in need and pray for them.

gifts.text: Presentation of the Gifts. What is happening? Bread and wine are brought to the altar. We offer our lives to God, too. Why do we do this? We thank God for his gifts. Try it! Think of one kind thing you can offer God today.. Big word: Altar. The holy table where the Eucharistic sacrifice is celebrated.

offerings.text: Prayer over the Offerings. What is happening? The priest prays over the gifts. We join his prayer and answer Amen. Why do we do this? We ask God to accept our offering. Try it! Listen and answer “Amen” with everyone.

eucharistic.text: Eucharistic Prayer. What is happening? The priest leads the great prayer of thanks to the Father. Jesus’ one sacrifice is made present at Mass. Why do we do this? We join Jesus in his offering to the Father. Try it! Listen with a quiet heart and give thanks to God.. Big word: Eucharist. The sacrament of Jesus’ Body and Blood; the word means thanksgiving.

sanctus.text: Holy Holy Holy (Sanctus). What is happening? We join the angels and saints in praising God. Together, we sing or say that God is holy. Why do we do this? We worship with the whole Church in heaven and on earth. Try it! Join in the words “Holy, Holy, Holy.”. Big word: Sanctus. A word that means holy.

consecration.text: Consecration. What is happening? By Jesus’ words and the Holy Spirit’s power, bread and wine become Jesus’ Body and Blood. Their look and taste stay the same. Jesus is truly present: Body, Blood, soul, and divinity. Why do we do this? Jesus gives us his whole self in the Eucharist. Try it! Adore Jesus quietly and say in your heart, “Jesus, I love you.”. Big word: Chalice. The sacred cup used at Mass.

amen.text: Great Amen. What is happening? The great prayer ends by giving glory to God. We answer with a strong Amen. Why do we do this? Our Amen joins us to the prayer. Try it! Say “Amen” clearly and joyfully.. Big word: Amen. A word that says yes to God: so be it.

ourfather.text: Our Father. What is happening? We pray the prayer Jesus taught us. We call God our Father and ask for what we need. Why do we do this? Jesus teaches us to trust our loving Father. Try it! Pray slowly with your family. Think about forgiving others.

peace.text: Sign of Peace. What is happening? We pray for peace and unity. We may share a simple sign of peace with those nearby. Why do we do this? We want to live as one family in Christ. Try it! Practice saying “Peace be with you” gently.

lamb.text: Lamb of God. What is happening? As the priest breaks the consecrated host, we call Jesus the Lamb of God. We ask him for mercy and peace. Why do we do this? Jesus gave his life to save us. Try it! Join the prayer with a gentle, listening voice.. Big word: Lamb of God. A name for Jesus, who offers himself to save us.

communion.text: Holy Communion. What is happening? Catholics who are prepared receive Jesus in Holy Communion. Jesus draws us closer to himself and to one another. Why do we do this? Jesus nourishes our life with him. Try it! Thank Jesus quietly. If you have not made First Communion, stay with your family and pray.

blessing.text: Final Blessing. What is happening? The priest asks God to bless us. We make the Sign of the Cross. Why do we do this? God helps us live our faith each day. Try it! Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and answer “Amen.”

dismissal.text: Dismissal. What is happening? The priest or deacon sends us out with words such as “Go in peace.” We answer “Thanks be to God.” We are ready to love God and serve others. Why do we do this? The Mass sends us to share Christ’s love. Try it! Practice answering “Thanks be to God” after “Go in peace.” Then choose one act of kindness to do today.

response-greeting.text: The priest says: The Lord be with you.

response-first.text: At the end of the reading, the reader says: The word of the Lord.

response-second.text: At the end of the reading, the reader says: The word of the Lord.

response-dismissal.text: The priest or deacon sends us forth with words such as: Go in peace.

explorer-altar.text: The altar is the holy table where the Eucharistic sacrifice is celebrated. At Mass, we gather around it to worship God.

explorer-ambo.text: The ambo is the special place where the Bible readings are proclaimed. We listen carefully to God’s Word.

explorer-candles.text: Candles give light in the church. Their light helps us remember Jesus, the Light of the world.

explorer-chalice.text: A chalice is the cup used at Mass. After the consecration, it holds the Precious Blood of Jesus.

explorer-tabernacle.text: The tabernacle is the special place where the consecrated hosts are kept. Jesus is truly present in the Eucharist. We can pray quietly to him here.

explorer-crucifix.text: A crucifix is a cross with an image of Jesus on it. It reminds us that Jesus gave his life to save us because he loves us.

explorer-paten.text: A paten is a small plate used to hold the host. After the consecration, the host is truly the Body of Jesus. We treat the Eucharist with great love and respect.
